lens.name: Fresh From arXiv
lens.brief: New preprints land every morning, and some have a figure or idea that can be played with. Pick a paper whose core mechanism fits in a browser and rebuild the intuition as an interactive, without claiming results you did not reproduce. Cite the abstract, show the toy, mark what is simplified.
sourceHints: arXiv new listings: cs.GT, cs.AI, cs.GR, physics.soc-ph, q-bio.PE, math.CO
r/MachineLearning and r/science weekly paper threads
Quanta Magazine and similar science journalism for context

lens.name: Chips Times Mult
lens.brief: Chips multiplied by mult is a tiny algebra that explodes: additive terms, multiplicative terms, retriggers, ordering effects, exponents. Make that math visible: an order-of-operations optimizer, a scoring-tree visualizer, a what-if explorer that finds the best joker order for a given hand.
sourceHints: r/dataisbeautiful and r/mathpics for ways to show combinatorial growth
Hacker News posts on game balance and numbers-go-up design

lens.name: Weird Web
lens.brief: The early-web spirit: strange sites that exist because someone had to make them. Build something form-breaking and art-adjacent, such as a page that reads you back, an interface that is also the content, or a cursor with a story. Not random for its own sake; it needs a rule you can feel.
sourceHints: Are.na channels on weird web and net art
Hacker News Show HN: strange websites

lens.name: Pun Engine
lens.brief: Language is a machine with loose parts. Build a toy that plays with them: anagram finders with taste, spoonerism makers, rhyme ladders, text rebranders that transform a paragraph into a different register. The wordplay needs real rules so the output keeps surprising.
sourceHints: Public domain word lists and corpora

lens.name: Instrument Maker
lens.brief: WebAudio makes the browser a synthesizer. Build an instrument or a composition engine with a distinctive way of playing: a physical-model string you pluck by drawing, a tuning-system explorer, a drum machine that evolves, a generative score that never repeats.
sourceHints: Wikipedia: Just intonation, Karplus-Strong string synthesis, Euclidean rhythm
Hacker News posts on WebAudio and procedural music

lens.name: Shareable Seeds
lens.brief: Design for the screenshot and the link: a seeded world, a daily challenge, a URL hash that reconstructs the exact state, a result card people want to send. The idea works alone but is better when passed around; make the share artifact beautiful and spoiler-safe.
sourceHints: Wikipedia: Procedural generation, Seed (random number generation)
Hacker News posts on daily-puzzle design

lens.name: Tonight on the Ice
lens.brief: What is the NHL talking about right now? A playoff race, a scoring streak, a hot goalie, a rule dispute, a rivalry, a rookie. Turn the live storyline into something playable or explorable, with a bundled dated snapshot of the numbers so it still works offline and every fact carries its date.
sourceHints: NHL.com public scores, standings and stats pages
r/hockey daily and post-game threads, top of the week

lens.name: The Confidently Wrong Machine
lens.brief: A contraption that explains, predicts or classifies with total conviction and delightfully bad reasoning, but with a consistent internal logic you can learn. Parody the tone of automated certainty, not any real product. The player's goal is to understand how it thinks.
sourceHints: r/ProgrammerHumor and r/ChatGPT-style absurd-output threads (the pattern, not specific outputs)
